skill.name: review-my-diff
skill.description: Self-review your uncommitted or branch changes before opening a PR, with findings ranked by severity and backed by file and line evidence. Use when asked to review my changes, check my diff or get ready for review.
skill.summary: Review local or branch changes with prioritized findings, file references, and explicit verification results.
skill.author: agentkitco

content.user_title: Review Your Diff Before Opening a Pull Request
content.value_statement: Local changes can hide bugs, security gaps, and missing tests before human review. This skill guides an evidence-based review with prioritized findings and explicit verification results.
actual_capabilities: Inspect staged, unstaged, and branch changes using Git commands.
Read surrounding callers, tests, and configuration to evaluate risky changes.
Check correctness, safety, tests, compatibility, maintainability, and change scope.
Run existing quick tests, lint, and type checks, reporting exact commands and results.
Group findings into blockers, recommended fixes, and optional nits with file and line evidence.
Distinguish verified issues from suspicions and end with a readiness recommendation.
limitations: Requires repository access and command execution tools for Git inspection and project checks.
Does not edit files unless explicitly asked.
Does not guarantee exhaustive coverage; large diffs may be reviewed by directory.
Does not replace human approval, and checks may be skipped when unavailable or slow.

use_cases.title: Check Local Changes Before a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Review staged and unstaged changes for bugs, unsafe behavior, and missing tests before requesting feedback.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Contributor Branch
use_cases.description: Compare a contributor branch against its base and examine compatibility risks, surrounding callers, and test coverage.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Review Work on Large Changes
use_cases.description: Review a large diff by directory and separate blockers from smaller fixes, documenting coverage and unresolved questions.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Current Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged and unstaged changes before I open a pull request. Report prioritized findings with file and line evidence. Do not edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch against the default branch using the merge base. State the intended change and check correctness, safety, and compatibility. Do not edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Error Paths and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my diff with attention to error handling, input validation, and missing regression tests. Run available quick checks and separate verified problems from suspicions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Large Compatibility Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this large branch by directory, tracing affected callers, public interfaces, configuration, and migrations. Document coverage, skipped checks, blockers, and questions. End with a readiness recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess broad changes and review coverage.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: review a change that removes required input validation and adds no regression test.
output: Checks run: none; this illustrative scenario provides no runnable repository.
Blocker summary: required validation is missing, allowing invalid requests into processing.
Suggested fix: restore validation and add a regression test.
Recommendation: needs rework because invalid input is not rejected.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: review a small refactor where executed checks pass and inspection finds no actionable issue.
output: Intent: reorganize existing logic without changing behavior.
Checks run: the review lists the exact commands and passing results from the actual session.
Looks good: existing behavior and regression coverage are preserved.
Recommendation: ready for human review; this is not approval.

best_practices: State the intended behavior and confirm the comparison base before reviewing branch changes.
Use a trusted environment for project checks, since tests and development tools execute repository code.
Require file and line evidence, exact check results, and explicit disclosure of unreviewed areas.
anti_patterns: Requesting automatic approval or treating the recommendation as a substitute for human review.
Assuming a review edits files or fixes reported issues without an explicit request.
Accepting unsupported findings or assuming that unreported tests passed.

faq.question: Which changes can this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews staged and unstaged changes, or compares a branch against its merge base with the default branch.

faq.question: Does it modify my files?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit editing files unless you ask. Project checks can still produce artifacts or other effects.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: It runs existing tests, lint, and type checks when they are quick. It must report commands, results, and skipped checks.

faq.question: How are findings organized?
faq.answer: Findings are grouped into blockers, recommended fixes, and optional nits. Each finding must identify a file, line, consequence, and suggested fix.

faq.question: Can it handle a large diff?
faq.answer: It can review large diffs by directory and must disclose that approach. Coverage is not guaranteed to be exhaustive.

faq.question: Does a ready recommendation approve my pull request?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly avoids approval and provides a readiness recommendation with reasons for human review.
